newsitem.title: UK: Metals end LME off highs, pause and watch copper.
newsitem.headline: Metals end LME off highs, pause and watch copper.

text.p: Base metal prices remained below earlier highs during Wednesday afternoon LME trading, as markets paused for breath in line with copper, traders said.
Copper hit a five-month high in early trading, pulling aluminium to its highest for 2-1/2 months and zinc moved above $1,080 to its best levels for 6-1/2 months.
But with little physical business to back the moves up, most markets subsequently subsided.
"The prices have been jumping around, but there has not been a lot of volume. The business has been fund short-covering, mostly," one trader said.
Copper peaked at $2,240 a tonne, but then backed away as lending against cash/threes cut into the backwardation, defusing some of the tightness.
Also, there was talk that the long run of inventory declines, which has brought LME stocks down to the lowest since June 1990, could be drawing to a close.
Many traders expect to see stocks start accumulating from the start of next month, and end-year levels may be some 20,000/30,000 tonnes above current levels.
In the short-term copper will remain unpredictable, but with charts looking overbought there may be a downside price reaction under $2,200 - an area that was supported today.
Final three months kerb business was at $2,215, down $10 from Tuesday's kerb. The cash/threes backwardation was around $135/145 against yesterday's $155/160.

Aluminium was supported around $1,500, having earlier hit a high of $1,510, with the market seeing some consumer interest and forward buying. But the scale of current price moves leaves the market vulnerable to a reaction near $1,520.
"That has been a sizeable move for aluminium - it could be limited on the upside now," one trader said.

In the background January date tightness narrowed the overall cash/threes contango to around $20 from $22/23 on Tuesday, with spreads seen contracting further. Final three months business was at $1,508, up $42.
Zinc encountered some profit-taking after running up to a $1,085 high on fund buying and buy-stops. Additional price gains depend on copper movements, and last business was at $1,077, still up $15.
Nickel attempted to steady itself after wide price fluctuations earlier this week. Prices are looking to build a base above $6,800, closing at $6,850, down just $10.
Tin inched higher in undramatic trading, largely reflecting copper's recent strong price performance. Last kerb trade was at $6,090, up $50.
Lead was helped by buying on dips under $700, and closed at $704, up $1. Alloy was marked higher with primary, finishing at $1,350/55.
